headline: Wet, windy weekend with a strong Saturday storm; cooler, drier weather next week.
summary: A series of Pacific storm systems is aimed at western Washington. A stronger one arrives Saturday, followed Sunday night by a cooler dip in the jet stream high in the atmosphere. After that, the storm track is expected to shift south of the area, and high pressure aloft should bring drier weather later in the week. Through Sunday expect wet, breezy conditions, with the strongest winds along the coast, in the low gaps through the Cascades, and near the eastern Strait. Heavy rain could flood the Skokomish River, and high tides will keep bringing minor to moderate coastal flooding. Monday turns noticeably cooler, with snow levels, the elevation where snow falls, near 4,000 feet. The rest of the week looks mostly dry, cool, and foggy at times, though forecasters are less sure about a midweek system because models keep shifting its track south.
changes: The earlier discussion was highly confident about strong gusts on the coast Saturday, but the later one says forecasters are less sure of Saturday's wind strength and are still weighing whether it warrants new headlines. Coastal flood advisories, a Storm Watch for the outer coast, and a Gale Watch for the Strait and northern inland waters were also added.
